lessons.name: What is an Operating System?
lessons.desc: An OS is software that manages computer hardware and provides services to programs. Without it, every app would need to talk to hardware directly. Examples: Linux, Windows, macOS, Android, iOS.
lessons.q: What is an operating system and why do we need one?
lessons.qsub: What would happen if there was no OS and two programs both tried to write to the disk at the same time?
terms: Wo software jo computer ke hardware (CPU, memory, disk) aur aapke programs ke beech setu ka kaam karta hai.
Computer ki wo cheez jo kaam aati hai — CPU ka time, memory, disk, keyboard, screen.
Jahan OS khud chalta hai — hardware par poori pakad.
lessons.what:
Computer ka asli badan (hardware) hai — CPU, RAM, disk. Par aap jaise chrome kholte ho, wo directly CPU/disk se baat nahi kar sakta.

Bich mein OS khada hai. Uska kaam: hardware ka time/resource sab programs ko baant dena, taaki har program ko lage ki wo akela hai. Short mein: OS = hardware ka manager aur programs ka dost.
lessons.analogy: Hotel ka manager. Saara staff (programs) khana banana chahta hai, par kitchen (hardware) ek hi hai. Manager tay karta hai kaun kab, kitni gas, kitna time use karega. Bina manager ke sab kahenge "pehle main!" aur kitchen tohde mein.
lessons.why: Agar OS na ho, to do programs ek saath disk par likhein — ek doosre ka data mita dein. Ya do teeno CPU pakad lein. OS isliye hai ki sab programs ko safe aur barabar time mile, aur koi doosre ka data na chheega.

where: "OS kya hota hai?" — hardware manager + programs ko time dena.
top/htop — OS har program ko kitna CPU/memory de raha hai.
Windows, Linux, macOS — sab "OS" hain, alag manager ki style.
pros: Hardware ke saath programs seedha nahi ulajhte.
Har program ko lagta hai wo akela chal raha hai.
Ek program ne garbadgi kari to poore computer ko nahi giraata (safety).
cons: OS bhi ek software hai — naya version upgrades mehnga.
Har kaam ke liye OS se request karna (syscall) ka thoda time lagta hai.
OS ke andar bugs = poore system par asar.
gotchas: Bas Itna Yaad: OS khud biryani nahi banata, wo chef hai jo raw bahan (CPU, RAM) ko pakar kar service karta hai.
"Linux sirf kernel hai, Ubuntu pura OS hai" — interview mein ye farak bolo.
OS ka asli kaam = process, memory, files, devices ko sanbhalna.

lessons.name: Types of Operating Systems
lessons.desc: Batch OS (jobs queued, no interaction), Time-sharing OS (multiple users share CPU, e.g. Linux), Real-time OS (hard deadlines, e.g. flight systems), Distributed OS (across machines), Mobile OS (Android, iOS).
lessons.q: What are the different types of operating systems? Give a real-world example of each.
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between a general-purpose OS and a real-time OS? Why can you not use Linux to control a pacemaker?
terms: Kaam pehle jama kar, phir ek saath process karo — koi interaction nahi.
Ek CPU ko kai users mein chhota-chhota time dekar sabko "apna" lagwana.
Pakki deadline — agar miss hui to disaster.
Kai computer milkar ek saath kaam karein, user ko lage ek hi ho.
Chhota-device (phone/tablet) ke liye bana OS — Android, iOS.
lessons.what:
OS alag-alag kaamo ke liye bane hain. Type usi se tay hota hai — kaun si baat sabse zaroori hai.

Batch — kaam pehle jama karo, machine ek saath process kare, result do. (Purana card-punching wala zamaana.)

Time-sharing — aapke desktop PC wale OS. Kai users/programs, har ek ko thoda time, sabko lagta main hi hoon.

Real-time — pakki deadline. Ek monitor ko 2 ms mein answer chahiye, warna patient ko khatra.

Baki Mobile (power-bachat, touch) aur Distributed (kai machines milkar ek saath).
lessons.analogy:
Restaurant ke do modes:
• Batch — aapne order likhke de diya, kitchen saare orders jama karke ek saath bana dega, tab hi plate milegi.
• Time-sharing — ek hi chef, har table ke order ko thoda-thoda banata hai, sabko lagta hai unka bhi ban raha hai.
• Real-time — ICU mein jab monitor beep kare, nurse ko turant aana hi hai — deri ki gunjaish nahi.
lessons.why: Ek OS sabke liye nahi bhai. Bank ka server ko zyada uthane chahiye (throughput). ICUs / flights ko pakka correct time chahiye. Isliye alag OS — har kaam ki apni pehli zaroorat.

Distributed = ek bade computer jaisa shaktishali.
cons: Batch slow, koi interaction/back-and-forth nahi.
Real-time me hardware/software dono mehngi (pakki honi chahiye).
Distributed me pareshaani: sync, network fail.
gotchas: Bas Itna Yaad: Time-sharing = sabko chhota-chhota time, Real-time = ek pakka time.
"Linux use karke heart-pacemaker nahi chala sakte" — kyunki general OS me deadline missing ho sakti hai.
Interview: "difference general vs RTOS?" = deadline hi asal jawab.

lessons.name: Kernel — The Core of the OS
lessons.desc: The kernel is the core program that runs at all times. It manages CPU, memory, devices, and files. User space = where your apps run. Kernel space = where the OS runs. Apps cannot touch hardware directly — they ask the kernel.
lessons.q: What is the kernel? What is the difference between user space and kernel space?
lessons.qsub: What are CPU privilege levels (Ring 0 vs Ring 3)? Why does the hardware enforce this separation?
terms: OS ka dil — hardware se seedha baat karta hai, har waqt memory mein rahta hai.
Jahan aapke apps chalti hain (Internet browser, games).
Jahan OS chalti hai — hardware par full control.
CPU ka batawara — kaun kitni taaqat use kar sakta hai (Ring 0 = OS, Ring 3 = app).
lessons.what:
OS poori koi ek cheez nahi — uske beech ka dil hai kernel. Restaurant ke staff mein head-chef.

CPU ke andar ek rule hai: aapke normal program (app) ko low privilege milta hai — wo hardware ko seedha nahi chhoo sakta. Sirf kernel, jo high privilege me chalta hai, hardware seedha use karta hai.

Jab app ko hardware chahiye (disk likho), wo kernel se request karta hai. Usi ko system call kehte hain.
lessons.analogy: Rail station par TCO (Train Control) wala bada officer. Driver (app) signals seedha nahi badal sakta. Wo TCO ko "mujhe font par jana hai" kehkar request karta hai — TCO (kernel) hi track badalta hai. Isi liye do drivers ek hi track par nahi aate.
lessons.why: Safety ke liye. Agar har app hardware ko seedha chhhoo sakta — ek app galti se poore computer ka data mita dega. Kernel hai kiwoon ke wo check-kar-ke deta hai — "tujhe ye file allowed hai ya nahi."

where: Ki Linux kernel, Windows NT kernel — har OS ka dil.
Ring 0 vs Ring 3 — isi se app ko internet band kiya jaata hai.
"user space vs kernel space?" — isi se seedha farak bolo.
pros: Hardware par seedha control — tez aur powerful.
Apps ko hardware ki jhanjhat se bachata hai (safe).
Kai apps ek hi hardware share kar sakti hain.
cons: Kernel ke bug = poora system crash.
System call ka overhead (har request par time).
Kernel khud complex aur bhaari hai.
gotchas: Bas Itna Yaad: Kernel = OS ka dil, high privilege, hardware usi ke haath. App = low privilege, request karta hai.
"Abhi wo kernel space vs user space hai" — Ring 0 vs Ring 3 bolne se sahi lagta hai.
Kernel par apna code chalaana (module) = poore system ko khatra.

lessons.name: System Calls — How Programs Talk to the OS
lessons.desc: A system call is how a user program requests a service from the kernel. Examples: open() (open a file), read() (read data), write() (write data), fork() (create a process), exit() (terminate). Every file operation, network call, or memory allocation goes through a syscall.
lessons.q: What is a system call? Why do we need them — why can't programs access hardware directly?
lessons.qsub: What is the cost of a system call? What happens at the CPU level when a syscall is made (trap/interrupt mechanism)?
terms: App ka kernel se request — "ye hardware ka kaam karke do".
Wo hardware-darwaaza jisme app kernel ke paas jaata hai (Ring 3 se Ring 0).
App ka data save, kernel ka load, phir wapas.
lessons.what:
Jab app ko koi OS ka kaam karna hai — file kholo, data padho, naya process banao, time pata karo — to wo seedha khud nahi kar sakta (low privilege). Wo system call karta hai.

Jaise read() dikhe to waise samjho: app kernel se mang raha hai "ye file se data de do". Kernel kehata hai, padhata hai, app ko result deta hai.
lessons.analogy: School mein peon pass: bachcha (app) library jaana chahta hai, par khud nahi jaa sakta. Wo teacher (kernel) se pass leta hai — wo check karta hai ki allowed hai ki nahi, phir bachcha jaata hai. Har bade kaam ke liye teacher ki ajeet hi chahiye.
lessons.why: Agar har app khud file/disk/network par poora control kar le, to wo doosre ka data beha sakta hai ya hardware todh de. System call rukawat hai — kernel har request check karke hi deta hai (allowed? safe?). Isi se security + safety dono milti hai.

pros: Hardware ka use controlled aur safe.
App ko hardware detail nahi sanbhalni padti.
Kernel har request check karta (permission).
cons: Har syscall ka overhead — context switch+boundary.
Kai syscall to program dhire ho sakta hai (batching).
Syscall ko qaada samajhne ka thaka (privacy, data copy).

"Why syscall costly?" = Ring 3→Ring 0 switch + data copy + back.

lessons.name: Computer Boot Process
lessons.desc: Power on → BIOS/UEFI (hardware check, find boot device) → Bootloader (GRUB loads kernel) → Kernel (initializes drivers, mounts filesystem) → Init/systemd (starts system services) → Login shell / Desktop. This is what happens before you see the login screen.
lessons.q: Explain what happens from the moment you press the power button to when the OS is ready.
lessons.qsub: What is BIOS vs UEFI? What is a bootloader? What is MBR vs GPT? What does systemd do?
terms: Computer ke "jaag-te" ka pahla software — abhi OS nahi chala.
Chhoti program jo kernel ko memory me load karke chalati hai (GRUB).
Kernel jab chalta hai — drivers, filesystem, memory set karta hai.
OS pehli service — baaki saare background processes isi ke bachchhe.
Naya BIOS — fast, safer (secure boot). BIOS purana.
lessons.what:
Power dabao → shuru se OS ready hone tak ek line hota hai:

1. Power on → BIOS/UEFI hardware check karta (RAM/disk on), boot device dhundta hai.

2. Bootloader (GRUB) — kernel ko disk se nikaal kar memory me daalta hai, phir chalata hai.

3. Kernel — khud shuru: drivers (keyboard, disk) load, filesystem mount (disk ko ready), memory setup.

4. init/systemd — pehla user-space process; phir baaki sab services (wifi, sound) isi ke children.

5. Login screen — ab aap aa sakte ho.
lessons.analogy:
Subah uthne ka kram:
1. Uthte hi check — paani hai, bijli hai (BIOS).
2. School bag nikaalo — jo kitabein chahiye (bootloader kernel uthata).
3. Teacher aata hai class sanbhalne (kernel init).
4. Monitor/bacche register hote hain (systemd) baaki services shuru.
5. Bell — aap kaam par lage (login).
lessons.why: Kyunki computer seedha OS nahi chhod sakta — hardware apne aap OS ko nahi bula leta. CPU ko pahle ye tay karna hota hai: kya karna hai, disk se kernel kahan milega, memory kaise set hogi. Ye kram fix karta hai ki sab sahi order me ho — warna computer khud hi kharab ho jaata.

lessons.name: Process vs Thread
lessons.desc: A process is an independent program with its own memory. A thread is a lightweight execution unit within a process sharing memory.
lessons.q: What is the difference between a process and a thread? What resources does each own?
lessons.qsub: Why is creating a thread much cheaper than creating a process? What does fork() do under the hood?
terms: Ek program jo memory mein chal raha hai. Uska apna ghar (memory), apna kagaz (files), apna sab kuch.
Process ke andar ka ek kaam-gunda. Ek process ke andar kai threads, sab ek hi ghar mein rehte hain.
Jab kai threads ek hi cheez ko chhoo rahe hon, phir bhi sab theek chale.
lessons.what:
Process = ek chhota sa "ghar" jisme program rehta hai. Agar do programs chalao to do alag ghar — ek ko pata nahi doosre ke ghar mein kya hai.

Thread = usi ghar ke andar ka kaam karne wala log. Ek ghar mein kai log (threads) reh sakte hain, sab ek hi kitchen (memory) share karte hain.

Farak bas itna: process ghar ko share nahi karta, thread ghar share karta hai.
lessons.analogy: Barish ka din — ek ghar mein 3 bhai (threads). Teeno ka kitchen same hai, isliye ek ne chai banayi to teeno chai peeyenge. Ab ghar ke bagal wala padosi (doosra process) — uska kitchen alag, hum nahi chhoo sakte.
lessons.why: Web page ek process hai. Agar poora web page ek hi insaan sambhalta to ek heavy kaam par page jam jaata. Isliye browser multiple threads rakhta hai — ek thread UI sambhalta hai, doosra network.

lessons.name: Process Control Block (PCB)
lessons.desc: Data structure the OS maintains for each process — PID, state, CPU registers, memory maps, open files.
lessons.q: What information is stored in a Process Control Block? Why does the OS need it?
lessons.qsub: When a context switch happens, what exactly gets saved and restored?
terms: Har process ka apna number (ID card number jaisa).
Process Control Block — OS ka register jisme har process ki poori history likhi rehti hai.
CPU ke andar ke chhote dabbe jahan abhi chalke hua data rehta hai.
lessons.what:
OS ko har process ki poori jankari rakhni padti hai — naam nahi, sab. Ye jankari ek packed file mein rehti hai, usi ko PCB kehte hain.

Jab koi process banta hai (app khulta hai), OS use ek PCB deta hai — jaise school mein admission par ek file banti hai.
lessons.analogy: School ka dafatar har bachche ki ek file rakhta hai — naam, roll no, marks, kya danda khaaya. Jab bachcha (process) kaam kar raha ho, uski poori poori file dafatar (OS) ke paas hoti hai.
lessons.why: CPU ek process chhod ke doosre par jaata hai (context switch). Jab wapas aata hai, use pata hona chahiye kahan se chhod ke gaya tha. PCB hi wo note hai — "yahan se chhod tha, yahin se uthao."

CPU ko pata rehta hai kahan se resume karna hai.
Debugging/management aasaan.

PCB list ko hi manage karna ek kaam hai.

lessons.name: Context Switching
lessons.desc: The OS saves the current process state and loads another process state — enables multitasking but has overhead.
lessons.q: Explain context switching. What is its cost and how can it be minimized?
lessons.qsub: Why is context switching between threads cheaper than between processes? What is a thread-local storage?
terms: CPU ka ek process chhod ke doosre par jaana — aur wapas aane ka rasta yaad rakhna.
Wo "kahaan hain" — save ki hui state jahan se resume karna hai.
Switch karne mein jo extra mehnat/time lagta hai.
lessons.what:
CPU ek waqt mein ek hi kaam karta hai. Par computer ko "sab ek saath chalta hai" dikhana hai.

Iski trick ye hai: CPU bahut tezi se ek process chhod, doosra pakad, phir pehla pakad. Har baar "chhodne" par wo note likhta hai — main yahan tak tha. Is note ko likhna aur doosre ka note padhna hi context switch hai.
lessons.analogy: Kai log ek saath kitabein padh rahe hain, par sirf ek chair hai. Har ek jab chair chhodta hai, apni book mein page par bookmark rakh deta hai. Haath badalne mein 2 second lagte hain (overhead), par sabko lagta hai sab padh rahe hain.
lessons.why: Iske bina aap ek app chalaoge to baaki sab freeze (ruk) jaayega. Context switch hi multitasking ka jadoo hai — switch itni tezi se hota hai ki aankh nahi pakadti.

Har tab ek process — tab switch par context switch hota hai.
"Multitasking kaise?" — answer isi switch ki tezi se hai.
pros: Ek CPU par bhi kai apps chalti hain.
Hara process ko thoda-thoda time milta hai.
User ko sab responsive lagta hai.
cons: Har switch par overhead (time waste).
Zyada switch = zyada waste — "context switch thrash".
Thread switch sasta, process switch mehenga (memory bhi badalni padti).
gotchas: Bas Itna Yaad: context switch = bookmark rukhna, doosre ki book uthana.
Process switch > thread switch overhead — kyunki process ki poori memory map badalni padti hai.

lessons.name: Process States
lessons.desc: New → Ready → Running → Waiting → Terminated. Understanding state transitions is key to debugging hung processes.
lessons.q: Describe the lifecycle of a process. Draw the state diagram and explain each transition.
lessons.qsub: What causes a process to move from Running to Waiting? Give three concrete examples.
terms: Kaam ke liye taiyar, par CPU abhi maujood nahi.
CPU iska kaam kar raha hai — iski baari.
Kisi cheez ka wait — input ya I/O ka. CPU ise chhod chuka hai.
lessons.what:
Har process ka ek chhota sa "jeevan" hota hai — kaafi phase jo ek ke baad ek aata hai:

New (bana) → Ready (taiyar, par number) → Running (CPU mila) → Waiting (kisi cheez ka wait) → Running wapas → Terminated (khatam).

Sabse zaroori transition: Running ⇄ Waiting. Jab process I/O ka wait karta hai (jaise file padh raha hai), CPU usse chhod kar doosre ko de deta hai.
lessons.analogy: Bank mein counter ek hai, log kai. Har log Waiting (queue) hai. Jab counter khaali to ek Running ho gaya. Agar usko passport copy chahiye (I/O) jo 2 min mein aaegi — to wo Waiting mein chala gaya, counter doosre ko mil gaya. Jab copy aayi, wapas queue.
lessons.why: CPU ko bekar baithna nahi hota. Jab ek process pareshan ho (I/O wait), use chhodkar doosre ko CPU de do. Isi se CPU "100% kaam" karta rehta hai, koi bekar nahi baithta.

CPU idle nhi rehta — I/O wait par doosre ko de do.
Diagram yaad rakhna easy — bass 4-5 boxes.
cons: State real hardware mein bhi isi waqt beech mein badal sakti hai (races).
Kai states aur transitions yaad rakhna muskil.
Real OS mein kai sub-states aur queues hote hain.

lessons.name: User-level vs Kernel-level Threads
lessons.desc: User threads managed by runtime library (fast, no syscall). Kernel threads managed by OS (can use multiple cores).
lessons.q: What is the difference between user-level and kernel-level threads? What are green threads?
lessons.qsub: Node.js uses a single kernel thread but handles concurrency. How? How does the thread pool in libuv help?
terms: OS khud banati hai — CPU cores taak jaa sakta hai. Bhaari, par matter hai.
Program ke andar ka thread — OS par nirbhar (diesel).
User thread jo runtime khud manage karti hai (JS/Python wale).
lessons.what:
Do thread ke do prakaar:

Kernel thread — OS khud banati hai. Use asli CPU core milta hai, kai cores par saath mein chalta hai. Banaane (syscall) ka thoda time lagta hai.

User thread — program ke andar ka, runtime sambhalta hai. Banaana sasta, chalaana fast — par agar ek kaam atak jaye (I/O), use aur risk ye hai ki poora program ruk sakta hai (ek thread atka to sab atke).
lessons.analogy: Kernel thread = apna banda OS se seedha baat karta hai, kai kaamon ko alag-alag cores par bhej sakta hai. User thread = ghar ke log jo khud samajh ke kaam baantte hain — fast, par agar ek log atak jaye (I/O) to poora ghar ruk sakta hai.
lessons.why: User thread isliye fast hai kyunki OS ko har baar poochna nahi padta. Kernel thread isliye zaroori hai kyunki use asli CPU cores milte hain. Dono ka balance chahiye.

gotchas: Bas Itna Yaad: user thread = runtime ka khilona (fast, ek hi jagah); kernel thread = OS ka banda (slow, cores milte hain).
JS single-threaded hai — par async I/O, network ab tak badhiya chalta hai kyunki woh "user thread" model hai.
Interview: "Node fast kyu? concurrency sab non-blocking." — yehi green thread hai.

lessons.name: fork() and exec()
lessons.desc: fork() duplicates a process; exec() replaces process image with a new program. Together: spawn a child process.
lessons.q: Explain fork() and exec(). What is copy-on-write and how does it make fork() efficient?
lessons.qsub: What is a zombie process? What is an orphan process? How do you prevent them?
terms: Process ki ek nayi copy banana — doosra process banna jaisi same program ki.
Us nayi copy ke andar purana program hata kar naya program daalna.
Sasta tariqa: copy sirf naam ki hoti hai, asli copying tabhi hogi jab kuch badala jaaye.
lessons.what:
Process ko naya kaam karna hai (jaise koi badhiya program chalana hai).

Do kaam karne padte hain:

1. fork() — apni ek "game ki copy" banaana (naya process). Ab do same program hain — parent aur child.

2. exec() — us nayi copy ke andar purana code hata kar naya program daalna. Child ka kaam alag ho gaya.

Milakar: nayi cheez chalu karni ho to fork karke exec karo.
lessons.analogy: Ek kitaab ki photocopy bana lo (fork) — ab do patti hain, same content. Phir ek patti ko faad kar usi par LIKH do nayi kitab ka content (exec). Photocopy sasti hai kyunki asli copying tabhi hoti hai jab kuch badlaav aaye (copy-on-write).
lessons.why: OS chahta hai naye program ke liye "sasti copy" ho te "nayi khali world" — khali world banana mehenga. Isliye pehle copy (fork, sasti), phir ek hisse ka daal badal karo (exec). Bas.

lessons.name: Stack vs Heap
lessons.desc: Stack: LIFO, fast, automatic, limited size. Heap: dynamic, manual (or GC), large, slower allocation.
lessons.q: Explain stack vs heap memory. What goes on each? What causes a stack overflow?
lessons.qsub: Why is stack allocation faster than heap allocation? What is memory fragmentation?
terms: Memory ka fast hissa — LIFO, automatic. Function call, local variables. Chhota (fixed size).
Memory ka bada hissa — dynamic, aap khud mangaate ho. Slow, par bada.
Stack khatam ho gaya — zyada deep recursion → crash.
Heap mein chhote-chhote khaali tukkde bikhre — naya bada block nahi milta.
lessons.what:
Ek program chalti hai to use memory do hisson mein milti hai:

Stack — sabse fast. Har function call par ek "tikki" (frame) upar rakha jaata hai, wapas hote hi hata deta hai. LIFO (last in, first out) — ek hi ke upar ek. Automatic, koi khud delete nahi karta.

Heap — sabse bada. Yahan aap khud memory maangte ho (object, array) kisi bhi order mein. Slow, aur khud free karna padta hai (GC ya manually).
lessons.analogy:
Plate ki dheri (stack) — hamesha upar rakho, upar se utaro. Fast aur fixed.
Store-room (heap) — koi bhi saman kisi bhi corner mein rakho, jab chahiye tab le lo. Badi jagah, par order ka koi niyam nahi — kai jagah khaali jagah bikhri padi ho.
lessons.why: Stack isliye fast hai kyunki waise hi simple hai — bas upar rakho/upar se hatao, koi note-keeping nahi. Heap isliye hai ki bade & dynamic data (jise size pehle se nahi pata) wahan aa sake. Dono ka apna kaam — isliye dono alag.

pros: Stack: tez, automatic, access karna sasta.
Stack: koi addressing strategy nahi (fixed).

cons: Stack: chhota — zyada deep recursion crash.
Heap: slow allocation, aur free hona zaroori (leak).
Heap: fragmentation — khaali jagah bikharti hai.

Primitives chhoti aksar stack, new/objects heap — par ye implementation detail hai.
Interview: "why stack faster?" — kyunki LIFO, addressing simple, cache-friendly.

lessons.name: Virtual Memory
lessons.desc: Each process sees its own private address space. OS maps virtual addresses to physical RAM using page tables.
lessons.q: What is virtual memory? How does it enable process isolation and allow programs larger than physical RAM?
lessons.qsub: What is address space layout randomization (ASLR) and why does it improve security?
terms: Jo pata program ko dikhta hai (jaise 0x4000) — real nahi.
Asli RAM ka pata — jo hardware par hota hai.
Chhoti book — har virtual pata ko physical bata-ti hai.
Har program ka apna alag area — doosra nahi chhoo sakta.
lessons.what:
Har program ko lagta hai ki uski poori RAM sirf usi ki hai — jaise 0 se 4GB tak, sab uska.

Par ye jhooth hai. OS virtual address space banata hai — ek fake, safe, bada space jahan program khelta hai. Asli RAM kahin aur hoti hai.

Page table wo translator hai jo bata-ti hai: "tumhara 0x4000 wala data asli RAM ke 0x9000 par hai." Program ko real duniya se koi fark nahi padta. Isi se isolation milta — ek program doosre ki memory ko dekh hi nahi sakta.
lessons.analogy: Bade warehouse (RAM) mein kai log alag-alag shelves pe kaam karte hain. Sabko ek map (page table) diya gaya hai ki uski cheez kahan hai. Na koi doosre ki shelf ko dekh sakta (isolation), na asli layout se pareshan. Aur agar cheez warehouse se bahar (disk) padi hai, map baad mein bata dega "ab mili" (page fault).
lessons.why: Do bade faayde: (1) Isolation — ek program ki galti doosre ka data nahi chhedti. (2) Badi programs — program se bhi badi program dikhti hai, kyunki jo hissa use nahi ho raha wo disk par reh sakta (agar RAM se bhi zyada chahiye).

"program 4GB RAM se bada kaise? " — virtual memory + disk.
pros: Isolation — ek program doosre ka data nahi chhedta.
Program choti RAM par bhi bada kaam kar sakta hai.
Har program ko "poori RAM" dikhti — simple.
cons: Har access par page-table lookup ka time lagta (TLB se theek).
Page fault slow — disk se uthana.
Page tables khud memory khaati hain.
gotchas: Bas Itna Yaad: virtual = jhootha bada pata, physical = asli RAM. Bich mein page table.
"Program ne 2GB memory li" — wo virtual ho sakta hai, asli kam.
Interview: "ASLR kya?" — random virtual addresses se attack mushkil.

lessons.name: Paging & Page Tables
lessons.desc: Physical memory divided into fixed-size frames. Virtual memory divided into pages. Page table maps pages to frames.
lessons.q: Explain paging. What is a page fault and how is it handled?
lessons.qsub: What is the TLB (Translation Lookaside Buffer)? Why is it critical for performance?
terms: Virtual memory ka chhota hissa (fixed, e.g. 4KB).
Asli RAM ka utna hi chhota hissa.
Wanted page RAM mein nahi — disk se uthana pada (slow).
Chhoti fast cache of page table — recent translations.
lessons.what:
Memory ko chhote-chhote same-size blocks mein kato (jaise book ke pages). Virtual side ke block ko page kehte hain, physical (RAM) side ke block ko frame.

Page table bata-ti hai ki kaunsa page kaunse frame mein padi hai. Jab program kisi page ko chhoo-ta hai jo RAM mein nahi (disk par hai), to page fault hota — OS disk se utha ke RAM mein daal deta, phir program chalta hai.
lessons.analogy: Library me har kitaab ke pages ko drawers mein rakhte ho — har drawer ka number (frame). Register (page table) rakhte ho ki jaise "page 5 = drawer 3". Jab koi page manga aur wo drawer mein nahi (store room/disk mein hai), to usse waha se laana padega (page fault) — time lagta.
lessons.why: Paging gives isolation + flexibility. Program ke saare pages RAM mein hona zaroori nahi — jo chahiye wo load. Isi se choti RAM par bhi bade program chalti hain. Aur fixed-size blocks se external fragmentation khatam (koi bada khali hissa dhundhni nahi padti).

lessons.name: Segmentation
lessons.desc: Memory divided into logical segments (code, data, stack). Each segment has base + limit registers.
lessons.q: What is segmentation? How does it differ from paging? What are its advantages and problems?
lessons.qsub: What is external fragmentation? How does paging eliminate it but introduce internal fragmentation?
terms: Memory ka logical hissa — code, data, stack, etc. (koi ek hissa).
Segment ka shuru hone ka pata (RAM).
Segment ki lambai — kitna bada hai.
Bikhri khaali jagah — nayi segment ke liye ek saath badi jagah nahi milti.
lessons.what:
Paging ne memory ko fixed blocks mein kato, par segmentation logical hisson mein kato — code, data, stack alag-alag segment.

Har segment apna base (kahaan shuru) aur limit (kitna lamba) rakhta hai. Program ka pata aisa likha hota hai: (segmentNo, offset). Hardware check karta — agar offset < limit nahi, to segfault!

Paging ki tarah blocks fixed nahi, chhoti-badi segment — isliye external fragmentation aati hai (bikhri khaali jagah).
lessons.analogy: Paging = sab drawers ek saath size ke. Segmentation = har cheez apne alag khaane mein — recipe ka ek dabba, masale ka ek dabba, sabzi ka ek dabba. Har dabbe ka apna size aur label (base+limit). Agar naya bada dabba rakhna hai aur beech-beech mein khaali jagah baqi nahi to problem (fragmentation).
lessons.why: Logical grouping: program ye jaanta hai ki code, data, stack alag hain — segmentation se wo structure memory mein bhi milta. Aur har segment ki apni limit ho, isliye agar program galat offset access kare to turant error (segfault) — data corruption se bachav. Par dikkat: sizes alag, to khaali jagah bikharti hai.

"segmentation vs paging" — logical vs fixed, ext vs int frag.

Limit se galat access turant pakda jaata (segfault).
Sharing — do process ek segment share kar sakte.

Har segment ki lambai yaad rakhna / allocate karna.

lessons.name: Page Replacement Algorithms
lessons.desc: When RAM is full and a new page is needed, the OS must evict one. FIFO, LRU, LFU, Clock algorithm.
lessons.q: Explain LRU page replacement. What is Belady's anomaly?
lessons.qsub: Why is LRU difficult to implement in hardware? What is the Clock algorithm and why is it a practical approximation?
terms: Wanted page RAM mein nahi — uthana pada.
Sabse pehle aaya wala hatao. Simple, par galat ho sakta hai.
Least Recently Used — sabse kam time pe use hua hatao. Best, par mehenga.
FIFO mein frames badhane par bhi zyada faults — ulta!
LRU ka sasta approximation — hardware friendly.
lessons.what:
Jab RAM bhar jaati hai aur naya page chahiye, OS ko ek purana page hata kar nikaalna padta hai. Kaunsa nikale? Yahi page replacement strategy hai.

FIFO — sabse pehle bhar aaya wala hatao. Simple par achha nahi.

LRU — sabse kam recent use hua hatao. Best, kyunki jiski zaroorat abhi nahi hogi wahi nikalo. Par asli hardware mein time-track karna mehenga.

Clock — LRU ka practical version: har page pe ek "use bit". Sab pages circle mein, jiska bit 0 ho use karo, warna clear karke aage.
lessons.analogy:
Office ka paper tray full hai; naya paper rakhna hai to kaun nikale?
• FIFO: jo sabse pehle rakha tha usi ko nikaal do (chahe wo abhi use ho raha ho).
• LRU: jo sabse kam time mein use hua ho (aur ab zaroorat nahi lag rahi) use nikaal do — zyada samajhdaari.
lessons.why: Agar galat page nikala (jo abhi chahiye hoga), to turant wo wapas fault karega — aur system baar-baar page-fault mein aa jaata hai: thrashing. Isliye sahi page nikala jaana zaroori hai — LRU style "ab nahi chahiye" waala nikalo.

FIFO simple, aasan implement.
Clock hardware-friendly LRU approximation.
cons: LRU exact mehenga — har access par track.
FIFO poori tarah Belady anomaly dikhai deti.
Clock approximate — perfect nahi.

lessons.name: Memory Leaks & Garbage Collection
lessons.desc: A memory leak is heap memory that is allocated but never freed. GC automates deallocation via reference counting or mark-and-sweep.
lessons.q: How do memory leaks happen in languages with and without GC? How do you detect them?
lessons.qsub: Explain the mark-and-sweep algorithm. What is a stop-the-world pause and why is it a problem for latency?
terms: Heap ki memory jo khud li gayi par kabhi free nahi hoti — program aage use ho raha hai.
Jo objects ab use nahi ho rahe, wo khud free kar deta.
GC ka tarika: root se jo sab reachable use mark karo; jo mark na hue wo free.
GC chalte waqt program ruk jaata — pause se latency.
Har object ke use-count; 0 hote hi free. (Cycles mein fail.)
lessons.what:
Leak = memory tumne li (allocate), par kabhi wapas nahi di jab wo use nahi rahi. Program chalta raha un object ko "pakad ke" rakhta hai.

GC waali languages mein (JS, Java, Go) GC khud dhundhta hai kaun ab use nahi ho raha (unreachable) aur free kar deta. Mark & sweep: root (global) se jaakar jo sab reachable unko mark karo; jo mark nahi hue wo free.

Par GC bhi leak nahi rok sakta agar object abhi bhi reachable ho (jaise global array mein bhi data).
lessons.analogy: Store-room mein koi naya saman le aata hai, par purana kabhi waste-bin mein nahi daalta. Saman (memory) ghar-ghar bhar jaata hai. GC ek cleaner hai jo dekhta hai "kaunsi cheez ab kisi kaam ki nahi (koi usse point nahi karta)" aur use phenk deta. Par agar saman abhi bhi kisi se linked hai, cleaner use nahi phenkega — aur yahi asli leak hai.
lessons.why: Leak se program ka memory dhire-dhire bhar jaata → degradation, crash, ya OS use kill kar de (OOM). Isliye samajhna chahiye: manual (C) mein khud free karna, GC mein reachability par depend. Aur closure/global hooks ko dhyaan rakhna.

Large in-memory cache bina eviction → OOM.
"GC leaks kese?" — reachable rehne par; cycles ref-count me.

Mark & sweep cycles handle karta (ref-count se zyada).
Reachability se clear model.
cons: Stop-the-world — GC pause par latency.
Leak tab bhi hota jab object reachable ho.
Ref-count cycles me leak (agar weak refs nahi).
gotchas: Bas Itna Yaad: leak = reachable memory jo kabhi hat-ti nahi. GC unreachable hi free karta.
JS: event listeners par addEventListener ro diya, remove bhul gaye → leak.

lessons.name: Scheduling Goals & Metrics
lessons.desc: Maximize CPU utilization and throughput. Minimize turnaround time, waiting time, and response time.
lessons.q: What are the goals of CPU scheduling? What trade-offs exist between throughput and latency?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between preemptive and non-preemptive scheduling?
terms: CPU kitna time busy rehta hai — kam khali na rahe.
Ek second mein kitne processes khatam hote hain.
Process shuru hone se khatam hone tak ka pura time.
Input dene se pehla output aane tak ka time — interactive systems mein important.
OS beech mein rok kar kisi aur ko CPU de sakta hai.
lessons.what:
Scheduler ka kaam: kaun sa process kab CPU chalaye. Par "best" ka matlab cheez-par-nirbhar hai — isliye goals define karte hain.

System goals: CPU busy rahe (utilization), zyada kaam ho (throughput). User goals: kaam jaldi khatam (turnaround), pehla jawab turant (response). In sab mein trade-off hai — ek goal badhao to doosra girt sakta hai.
lessons.analogy: Ek chef (CPU) ki kitchen zaada hai — kayi orders (processes) aate hain. Goals: kitchen kabhi khali na rahe (utilization), jitne ho orders serve ho (throughput), har order jaldi ready ho (turnaround), aur customer ko pehla bite jaldi mile (response). Sab ek saath nahi ho sakte — isliye chef decide karta hai ki is waqt kya zaroori hai.
lessons.why: Bina goals ke scheduler man-maani process chalata hai — kabhi kuch processes bhuke (starvation), kabhi CPU khali. Goals se designer decide karta hai kaunsa strategy use karna hai — background batch vs interactive desktop vs real-time, sabke goals alag.

Response time important — jaldi jawab mile.
"scheduling goals kya?" — utilization, throughput, turnaround, response.
pros: Clear goals se sahi algorithm chun sakte ho.
Trade-off samajh kar delay/throughput balance karte ho.
System vs user goals alag-pana batata hai ki kaun sa system hai.
cons: Ek goal ko optimize karo to doosre ko nuksan.
Real workloads mix hote hain — ek hi policy fit nahi.
Response vs throughput ka balance tricky.
gotchas: Bas Itna Yaad: utilization = CPU busy rahe, throughput = zyada kaam, turnaround = jaldi khatam, response = pehla jawab turant.
Preemptive = OS beech mein rokta hai; non-preemptive = process khud chhod ta hai.
Interview: "throughput vs latency" — dono alag, trade-off hai.

lessons.name: FCFS, SJF, SRTF
lessons.desc: First-Come-First-Served: simple, convoy effect. Shortest Job First: optimal avg wait, needs future knowledge.
lessons.q: Compare FCFS and SJF. What is the convoy effect? Why is SJF optimal but impractical?
lessons.qsub: What is starvation? How does aging solve it?
terms: First Come First Served — jo pehle aaya wo pehle (queue jaisa).
Ek lamba process sab ko piche rokh deta hai — traffic jam.
Shortest Job First — sabse chhota kaam pehle. Optimal avg wait.
Shortest Remaining Time First — preemptive SJF.
Chote processes aate rahein to lamba kabhi nahi chattas — bhuka reh jaata.
Purane processes ki priority badhao taaki bhuke na rahein.
lessons.what:
FCFS — sabse simple. Jo process pehle bazaar aayi usi ko CPU. Order = arrival order. Dikkt: ek lamba process aaye to uske piche saare lambe intezaar mein — convoy effect (traffic jam).

SJF — sabse chhota kaam pehle. Yeh average wait time ko optimal banata hai. Par problem: future nahi pata (kaun sa kitna lama hai), aur chhote aate rahein to bada starvation se bhukha mar jaata.

SRTF — SJF ka preemptive version: jab bhi naya chhota aata hai, chalti process ko rok kar use de do.
lessons.analogy:
Billing/ATM ki line:
• FCFS — jo pehle khada wo pehle. Agar saamne waale ka kaam 10 minute ka hai aur tumhare aage sab ka 1 minute, to tum 10 minute intezaar karoge (convoy).
• SJF — sabse pehle wo serve karo jiska kaam sabse chhota. Line tez khatam (optimal), par agar chhoote aate rahein to bade wale kabhi turn nahi paenga (starvation).
lessons.why: FCFS realistic to hai par wasteful (convoy). SJF average ke liye best hai par future prediction aur starvation ki problem. In dono se concepts clear hote hain — preemption, optimality, starvation, aging — jo baaki algorithms mein bhi use hote.

SRTF (preemptive SJF) response better deta hai par aur zyada overhead.

lessons.name: Round Robin
lessons.desc: Each process gets a fixed time quantum in a circular queue. Good for time-sharing systems.
lessons.q: Explain Round Robin scheduling. How does quantum size affect performance and response time?
lessons.qsub: What happens if the quantum is too large? Too small? What is the ideal quantum?
terms: Har process ko utna samay (ek "slice") CPU milta hai.
Circular queue — process time khatam hote hi piche lag jata.
Quantum khatam ho to OS rok kar agla laga deta.
Har switch par state save/restore ka time — overhead.
lessons.what:
Round Robin — har process ko ek fixed time quantum diya jaata hai, phir agla. Order circular hai — aakhri ke baad pehle wapas.

Har process ko barabar time milta hai — koi bhuka nahi rehta. Isliye interactive/time-sharing ke liye best. Par quantum chuno samajhdaari se: bahut chhota → zyada context switches (overhead), bahut bada → FCFS ban jaata.
lessons.analogy: Ek diet/round jisme chef har ek waiter ko ek jaisa 2 minute deta hai, phir agla. Sabko barabar mauka. Agar 2 min bahut chhota ho to chef baar-baar apna kaam rokta hai (overhead); bahut bada to pehla waiter sab kaam kha jaata (FCFS). Sahi balance chahiye.
lessons.why: Response time fair aur predictable chahiye to Round Robin best hai — koi process pat kayi second CPU pakad ke nahi rehta. Desktop/UI ke liye yehi chahiye: har app har waqt thoda-thoda comment. Time-sharing systems isi par chalti hain.

lessons.name: Priority Scheduling & Multilevel Queues
lessons.desc: Higher priority processes run first. Multilevel feedback queues adapt priority dynamically.
lessons.q: Explain priority scheduling with aging. What is a multilevel feedback queue?
lessons.qsub: How does Linux's Completely Fair Scheduler (CFS) work? What is the nice value?
terms: Har process ko ek number — zyada wala pehle.
Wait badhne par priority badhao — starvation rokne ke liye.
Kai queues (alag priority); process behaviour se queue badal sakta.
Linux ka scheduler — sabko fair CPU time (vruntime).
Linux mein priority adjust karne ka user-level knob (-20 to 19).
lessons.what:
Priority scheduling — har process ki ek priority hoti hai; sabse zyada priority wala pehle. Par risk: low-priority process kabhi CPU na paaye → starvation. Iska ilaj aging — jitna wait karna, utna priority badhao, taaki pahunch jaye.

Real system mein multilevel queues — alag-alag priority ki kai queues, har queue ki apni policy (front par RR, piche par FCFS). Aur feedback — agar process zyada CPU use kar raha (CPU-bound) to uski priority kam karo, taki interactive processes ko mauka mile.
lessons.analogy: Hospital emergency triage — jo critical (zyada priority) wahi pehle. Par agar sirf zyada-priority ke patients aate rahein, to kam-priority wala kabhi doctor nahi dekh sakta (starvation). Aging = "itte der intezaar kar liye, ab tumhe upar karo." Feedback = jo patient der tak ICU mein hai (long), usko general ward (low priority) shift karo taaki urgent logo ke liye jagah bane.
lessons.why: Real systems alag-alag process type chalti hain — interactive (UI, typing), batch (rendering, compile), background (downloads). Sabko ek jaisi policy dena galat. Priority + multilevel feedback se interactive ko response aur batch ko CPU-balance milta. Yehi Linux ka bhi model hai.

pros: Critical processes pehle — flushtable/urgent kaam.
Aging starvation rokta hai.

Priority misuse → high-prio hogmonopoly.

Linux CFS priority policy nahi, fair-share hai — sabko vruntime barabar.
Interview: "nice 19 vs -20" — lower nice = higher priority (weird but true).

lessons.name: Real-Time Scheduling
lessons.desc: Hard real-time: must meet deadlines (EDF, RMS). Soft real-time: best effort (multimedia, UI).
lessons.q: What is the difference between hard and soft real-time systems? What is Earliest Deadline First?
lessons.qsub: Why can't you use standard Linux for hard real-time systems? What is PREEMPT_RT?
terms: Deadline pakki — miss hui to disaster (safety-critical).
Deadline best-effort — miss hui to quality girti, disaster nahi.
Rate Monotonic — chhoti period wala high priority.
Earliest Deadline First — sabse jaldi deadline wala pehle. Optimal.
Linux ka real-time patch — preemption zyada, latency kam.
lessons.what:
Real-time = har kaam ki ek deadline hoti hai. Hard: deadline miss hui to fail (brake system, pacemaker). Soft: miss hui to quality girti (video call, game) — par system chalta rahta.

Algorithms: RMS — jaaldi repeat hone wala (chhoti period) high priority. EDF — sabse jaldi deadline waala hamesha pehle; ye optimal hai (agar koi schedule possible hai to EDF karega). Par EDF ko har waqt deadline track karni padti hai.
lessons.analogy:
Delivery company ka scheduler:
• Hard deadline: oxygen cylinder 2 ghante mein pahunchana hi padega — miss hui to patient ko khatra. Iske liye deadline pehle-rating (EDF).
• Soft deadline: pizza 30 min mein best-effort — 35 min pe bhi customer khush (thoda). RMS = jiski slot jaaldi-repeat, uski priority upar (jaise daily delivery route).
lessons.why: Normal scheduling (fair share) deadline ki parwah nahi karta — isliye real-time systems ko apna scheduler chahiye jo deadline guarantee de. Hard systems mein to guarantee hi jaan hai. EDF ka optimal hone ka proof isliye important hai — scheduler design ka funda.

cons: EDF mehenga — har waqt deadline sort.

Normal Linux scheduler real-time guarantee nahi deta — isliye PREEMPT_RT / RTOS.

lessons.name: File System Basics
lessons.desc: Files are named byte sequences. Directories are files that map names to inodes. Everything in Unix is a file.
lessons.q: How does a file system organize data on disk? What is the difference between a file, inode, and directory?
lessons.qsub: What is a hard link vs a soft link? What happens when you delete a file with multiple hard links?
terms: Bytes ka ek named sequence — data ko naam se rakho.
Khud bhi ek file — jo naam→inode ka map rakhta hai.
File ka "identity card" — metadata (size, permissions, data blocks).
Unix ka funda — file, disk, device, pipe sab file jaisa behave karta.
Root se file tak ka rasta — /home/user/a.txt.
lessons.what:
Disk par data raw bytes ki tarah pda hota hai. File system usko organise karta hai — files (named byte sequences) aur directories (jo files/dirs ko parent se jodti hain).

Har file ki ek inode hoti hai — usme file ka metadata (size, owner, permissions, disk par blocks kahan) hota hai, par naam nahi. Naam directory mein rakhta hai (naam → inode number). Isliye do names alag directory mein ek hi inode ki taraf point kar sakte hain (hard link).
lessons.analogy: Library ka card catalog: har book (file) ki ek entry (inode) hoti hai jisme details hain. Catalog mein (directory) naam se us entry ka number milta. Do catalog cards ek hi book ko bata sakte hain (hard links). "Everything is a file" = DVD player (device) bhi library ki ek entry jaisa — usme bhi read/write hota hai.
lessons.why: File system ke bina data ka koI organization nahi — sab raw. Inode+directory ka design named access, linking, permissions sab sambharta hai. "Everything is a file" Unix ka power hai — ek uniform interface se file, socket, device sab par kaam hota.

Inode+dir se linking & permission clean.
Everything-is-a-file = uniform interface.
cons: Files/flatten ke bina unorganised tarah.
Directory parhna bhi I/O — cache chahiye.
Metadata (inode) overhead.
gotchas: Bas Itna Yaad: file = named bytes. directory = naam→inode map. inode = metadata, naam nahi.
Hard link = do naam, ek inode. Soft link = alag file jo path point karta.
Interview: "delete karo aur ek hard link baaki — data nahi gayab" (ek inode, do naam).

lessons.name: Inodes
lessons.desc: An inode stores metadata about a file (size, permissions, timestamps, data block pointers) but NOT the filename.
lessons.q: What is an inode? What information does it store? What is the inode table?
lessons.qsub: Can you run out of inodes before running out of disk space? When does that happen?
terms: File ka metadata — size, perms, owner, timestamps, data-block pointers.
File ka unique ID filesystem ke andar.
Saari inodes ka area — disk par fix hota.
Kitne names is inode ko point karte hain.
Chhote data direct pointer; lamba data indirect blocks se (multi-level).
lessons.what:
Inode file ka metadata card hai — usme file ka content nahi, par file ke baare mein sab: size, owner, permissions, timestamps aur data blocks kahan hain. File ka naam yahan Nahi hota.

Har file ka ek inode number hota hai. Directory wo number + naam rakhti hai. Link count batata hai kitne names is inode ko point karte hain — delete par count 0 hone par hi data asli free hota.

Data blocks pointers: chhote file ke liye direct pointers. Bade file ke liye indirect pointers (pointer→block jo aur pointers rakhta) — isi se bada file bhi inode se manage hota.
lessons.analogy: Library book ka index card: uspar book ki info (size, shelf location) likhi hai, par book ka title (naam) card par nahi — woh catalog (directory) mein. Do do alag catalog entries ek hi index card ko point kar sakti hain (hard links). Cards ki total jagah (inode table) limit hai — khaali disk ho par cards khatam ho sakte hain (inode exhaustion).
lessons.why: Inode separate rakhne se naam aur metadata alag manage hote hain — isi se hard links, rename (sirf directory change), aur permissions ka clean model milta. Inode table ki samajh isliye zaroori ki disk space ho par inodes khatam ho sakte hain — ek common gotcha.

Bohot chhote files -> inode khatam (inode starvation).
pros: Metadata ek jagah — fast lookup (basic attrs).
Hard links & rename cheap (sirf directory change).
Direct/indirect flex — bade files bhi handle.
cons: Inodes limit — disk jagah ho par khali na hona.
Metadata update = inode write (journal).
Chhote files par inode overhead.

"Disk full but can't write" — ho sakta hai inodes khatam.
Interview: "delete file kabhi actually free?" — sirf jab last link remove + no process open.

lessons.name: File Descriptors
lessons.desc: An integer that represents an open file in a process. 0=stdin, 1=stdout, 2=stderr. File descriptor table per process.
lessons.q: What is a file descriptor? What happens when you open() a file?
lessons.qsub: What is the file descriptor limit per process? What is "too many open files" and how do you fix it?
terms: Ek integer jo process ke andar kholi hui file/device/socket ko represent karta.
OS-level — global open files ka record (offset, inode).
Per-process — kitne open fds hain, kis global file ko point karta.
FD limit khatam — ulimit -n se dekh/barha sakte.
lessons.what:
File descriptor ek integer hai — process apni kholi hui file ko is number se pehchanta hai. open() par OS ek naya fd deta hai (har process ki apni FD table).

Default: 0=stdin, 1=stdout, 2=stderr. Har fd one open file description ki taraf point karta (jo offset, inode rakhta).

FD limit hoti hai (ulimit). Server kai sockets kholta hai — "too many open files" tab aata jab FD table bhar jaati. Isliye fd close karna (resource), leak nahi karna.
lessons.analogy: Restaurant ka table number: tum (process) ko table 5 diya (fd). Waiter (OS) jaanta hai table 5 kya hai. Har din (process) apni apni table-numbers hoti hai. Limit: bhoot sarre tables na khul jaayein — kitchen (OS) thrott hai. Table bhool kar close nahi kiya (fd leak) to khali ho hi nahi sakti.
lessons.why: FD karne se isolation aur safety: process sirf apne fds par hi baat kar sakta — doosre ka nahi. Aur uniform: same read/write interface file, socket, pipe sab par. Layers jaise web server/Node isi par build hote hain (events + fds).

lessons.name: Journaling File Systems
lessons.desc: Log changes before applying them to ensure consistency after crash. Write-ahead logging. Used in ext4, NTFS, HFS+.
lessons.q: What is a journaling file system? How does it protect against corruption after a crash?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between data journaling and metadata-only journaling?
terms: Pehle "kya badalne wala hai" log karo, phir file system par lagao.
Badlav apply karne se pehle usko log karna.
Achanak power cut par file system corrupt na ho.
Sirf metadata (directory/inode) log; data blocks nahi.
lessons.what:
File system par kai writes ek saath honi hoti hain (inode + data block + directory). Agar power beech mein gayi, to kuch likha kuch nahi → corruption.

Journaling: badlav ko pehle ek log (journal) mein likho, phir asli jagah par. Crash hone par OS journal ko dekh kar ya to khatam karega ya waapas le jayega — consistent state.

Write-ahead: journal ka likhna hamesha data ke badlav se pehle — isi se guarantee. Metadata journaling (ext4 default) data ki jagah sirf metadata log karta — faster.
lessons.analogy: Formula 1 race mein har kaam pehle "right to repair/review" — HEADER mein likho ki kya change kar rahe. Crash = engine ruk gaya. Journal dekh kar pata chalta kya adha hua — usse complete / undo. Bina journal ke adha karne par record corruption. Like a to-do list: pehle list likho, phir kaam karo; bich mein ruke to list se pata chalta kya hua.
lessons.why: Data apke liye important hai. Crash / power cut aam hai. Journaling ke bina file system check (fsck) mein ghante lagte the aur data lost. Journal = speed vs safety: pehle log, phir apply — thoda slow, par crash-safe. Isi liye modern FS (ext4, NTFS) sab journaling hain.

lessons.name: Disk Scheduling Algorithms
lessons.desc: FCFS, SSTF (shortest seek time), SCAN (elevator), C-SCAN. Minimize disk seek time.
lessons.q: Explain SCAN (elevator) disk scheduling. Why is it better than FCFS for HDDs?
lessons.qsub: For SSDs, does disk scheduling matter? Why or why not?
terms: Read/write head ko correct track tak jaane ka time — HDD ka sabse bada cost.
Jo request pehle aayi turant serve — simple par seek zyada.
Shortest Seek Time First — sabse paas wala pehle.
Head ek side se doosri side jaata, raste ke requests serve.
Sirf ek direction mein serve, head wapas turant (uniform wait).
lessons.what:
HDD mein read/write head ek track se doosre tak jaana hai — isi ko seek kahte hain aur ye sabse slow. Disk scheduler requests ka order isi tarah lagata hai ki head kam ghoome.

FCFS — aate hi serve (simple, par head chaubhara). SSTF — sabse paas wala pehle (fast, par poori tarah optimal nahi). SCAN — head ek side se doosri jata, beech ke sab serve (elevator). C-SCAN — sirf ek direction, phir wapas (har jagah barabar wait).
lessons.analogy: Elevator gang SCAN: upar jaate waqt jo floor aate serve karta, chadke upar, phir niche. Isse koi floor behad intezaar nahi karta (starvation na). FCFS = elevator jaisi order aayi use hi jaata — baar-baar upar-neeche moot (seek zyada). SSTF = jo sabse paas floor use pehle — jabardast to fast, par door walon ko intezaar (poori starvation possible).
lessons.why: HDD slow hai to seek kam karne se I/O tez. Scheduling order sirf seek time optimize karta hai. Par fairness bhi chahiye (starvation na) — isliye SCAN/C-SCAN elevator style: both speed + fairness. SSD me seek time zero (no head), isliye scheduling bekaar zyada nahi.

SSTF starvation possible (door wala).

lessons.name: Pipes & Named Pipes
lessons.desc: Pipes: unidirectional byte stream between related processes. Named pipes (FIFOs): persist in filesystem, any two processes.
lessons.q: How do pipes work? What is the difference between anonymous and named pipes?
lessons.qsub: How does the shell pipe operator (|) work at the OS level?
terms: Unidirectional byte stream — ek process likhta, doosra padhta.
Filesystem mein naam se — koi bhi do process.
Pipe mein kernel ka temporary storage; agar bhar to writer block.
Ek side data daalta (in), doosri side nikalta (out).
lessons.what:
Pipe ek ek-disha (one-way) byte stream hai — ek process andar likhta hai, doosra bahar padhta hai. Order maintain hota (FIFO).

Anonymous pipe: parent-child ke beech — shell ka ls | grep isi par. Named pipe (FIFO): filesystem mein ek file jaisa naam, koi bhi do unrelated process jud sakte.

Pipe slow isliye kyunki data kernel buffer se guzarta hai (copy). Par safe — processes memory alag, isliye data bhejne ka aasan rasta.
lessons.analogy: Ek chhota pipe / nali: ek taraf aap paani (data) daalte ho, doosri taraf nikalta hai. Sirf ek direction. Kernel buffer = nali ke beech ka chhota godaam — agar bhar jaye to writer ko rukna padega (block). ls | grep = pipe operator dono ko jodta hai — ek ka output doosre ka input.
lessons.why: Processes ki memory alag hoti hai — direct share possible nahi. Pipe ek simple, safe rasta: data kernel ke through bheja jaata hai, koi race nahi. And shell scripting ka backbone — ek command ka output doosre mein feed.

Ordered & lossless — har byte ek baar, order me.

lessons.name: Shared Memory
lessons.desc: Fastest IPC — two processes map the same physical memory pages. Requires synchronization (semaphores/mutexes).
lessons.q: How does shared memory IPC work? Why is it the fastest IPC mechanism?
lessons.qsub: What synchronization mechanisms must accompany shared memory? What happens without them?
terms: Do (ya zyada) processes ek hi physical memory pages map karein.
Data hi share hai to races rokne ke liye mutex/semaphore chahiye.
Dono ek saath likhein to galat data — sync ke bina.
Kernel copy nahi — seedha memory, isliye sabse tez.
lessons.what:
Shared memory — do processes ek hi physical memory pages ko apni virtual space mein map karte hain. Jo ek likhta, doosra turant dekh sakta — bina kernel copy ke. Isliye yahi fastest IPC hai.

Par khudra sync chahiye: agar dono saath likhein → race condition. Isliye shared region ke saath mutex/semaphore use karo. Note: memory stack/heap ki tarah, ye alag physical pages par hota.
lessons.analogy: Do dost ek hi ghar (shared memory) mein rehte hain. Cheezein (data) ghar mein rakhi — koi copy ki zaroorat nahi (fast). Par agar dono ek saath kitchen (same data) use kaare, to hojam (race). Isliye rule/taala (mutex) — ek time par ek hi use kare. Shared ghar = super fast, par discipline zaroori.
lessons.why: Pipe har baar kernel copy karta hai — lamba data par slow. Shared memory direct access deta hai — bina copy, bina syscall (baad ki). High-throughput IPC (video buffers, analytics) ke liye yahi chahiye. Cost: aapko khud sync manage karna.

lessons.name: Message Queues & Sockets
lessons.desc: Message queues: asynchronous, typed messages. Sockets: network or Unix domain, bidirectional, flexible.
lessons.q: Compare message queues, shared memory, and sockets for IPC. When would you choose each?
lessons.qsub: What is a Unix domain socket? How does it differ from a TCP socket in performance?
terms: Typed messages ka queue — processes ek-doosre ki taraf push/recv.
Bhejne wala wait nahi karta — message queue mein jaata.
Har message ka ek type/label — selective receive.
Same machine — TCP jaisa interface, par kernel-local, fast.
lessons.what:
Message queue — processes structed messages bhejti hain (type + data). Bhejne wala wait nahi karta (async), OS queue mein rakhta. Alag tarike se: sockets — bidirectional byte connection, local (Unix domain) ya network (TCP).

Message queues decouple — producer/consumer alag speed; queue buffer. Sockets flexible — serve-request pattern, network bhi. Shared memory se slow par safe/simple.
lessons.analogy: Office mail system: tum box (message queue) mein note daalte ho, receiver baad mein aakar uthta hai — tum ruke nahi (async). Har note par type (e.g. "urgent") hota hai. Sockets = direct telephone line — do-way, turant, dono baat karte. Message queue = post office (async), socket = phone call (sync).
lessons.why: Jab processes ko data structure wise baat karni ho aur daau hi daalu na chahiye — message queue ideal. Jab request-response ya network ho — sockets. Ye IPC choices ka practical toolkit hai: speed (shared) vs convenience (message) vs flexibility (socket).

lessons.name: Signals
lessons.desc: Asynchronous notifications sent to a process — SIGINT (Ctrl+C), SIGKILL, SIGTERM, SIGSEGV.
lessons.q: What are signals in Unix? What is the difference between SIGTERM and SIGKILL?
lessons.qsub: Can you catch SIGKILL? What about SIGSTOP? How do you write a signal handler in C/Node.js?
terms: Process ko bheja gaya notification — hardware ya software event.
Forced kill — catch nahi hota, turant.
Rok / phir chalao — SIGSTOP nahi catch hota.
Signal par chalne wala function (jo aap define karte ho).
lessons.what:
Signal ek asynchronous notification hai jo OS process ko deta hai — "ye ho gaya" / "rok!" / "terminate". Jaise Ctrl+C → SIGINT.

Kuch signals catchable hain — aap handler likh kar cleanup kar sakte ho (SIGTERM). Par SIGKILL aur SIGSTOP catch nahi hote — OS force karta hai. Ye important: "kill" karne ka matlab hamesha SIGKILL nahi — kill <pid> default SIGTERM bhejta.
lessons.analogy: Boss (OS) tumhe (process) call/paigar bhejta hai: "theek ho?" (SIGUSR), "ab band ho jao grace se" (SIGTERM). Tum unhe handle kar sakte ho — cleanup, file close. Par agar boss bole "nikal turant" (SIGKILL) — tum kuch nahi kar sakte, seedha jaate ho. "Ruk jao" (SIGSTOP) bhi force. Ye paigar asynchronously aate — kab bhi.
lessons.why: Signals se OS process ko events bata sakta hai — user Ctrl+C de, process khud bgrund zyada kha le, ya shutdown process ho. Graceful shutdown (SIGTERM handler) se aap data commit / connection close kar sakte ho — isliye production code signal handlers rakhta hai.

lessons.name: Blocking vs Non-Blocking I/O
lessons.desc: Blocking: caller waits until I/O completes. Non-blocking: returns immediately, caller polls or is notified.
lessons.q: What is blocking vs non-blocking I/O? How does non-blocking I/O enable high-concurrency servers?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between non-blocking I/O, async I/O (AIO), and I/O multiplexing (select/poll/epoll)?
terms: Caller ruk jaata jab tak I/O khatam na ho — thread blocked.
Call turant return — agar data nahi to error/wait, caller poll karta.
Ek thread kai fds ko ek saath dekh sakta (select/poll/epoll).
OS khud complete karta — callback kyun?
Sink slow ho to source ko rukne ke liye signal.
lessons.what:
Blocking I/O: tum read() karo to thread ruk jaata jab tak data na aaye — simple, par ek thread per request (expensive).

Non-blocking I/O: read() turant return karta — data ready ho to de deta, nahi to "would block" bolta. Thread busy nahi rehta.

I/O multiplexing: ek thread select/epoll se kai fds monitor — "kaun ready hai?" — aur sirf ready wale par read. Yahi high-concurrency engines (Node, Nginx) ka base — ek thread hazaron connections.
lessons.analogy:
Restaurant ka server (thread):
• Blocking: server har ek table ke saamne khada rehta jab tak order ready — ek time par ek hi table (slow, many servers).
• Non-blocking + multiplexing: ek server order deta, turant agli table jaata; jab bhi kitchen "table 5 ready" (event) — usi table serve karta. Ek server, kai tables. Yahi Node/Nginx ka model.
lessons.why: Haaron kaam aata hai I/O wait — network, disk. Agar ek thread wait par rukta, to 10k connections = 10k threads = memory blast. Isliye non-blocking + multiplexing se ek thread par wait float hota — high concurrency, kam resources. Backpressure: jab sink slow to source pause — buffer blast na ho.

lessons.name: epoll / kqueue / I/O Multiplexing
lessons.desc: Monitor many file descriptors simultaneously without polling. The basis of Node.js, Nginx, Redis event loops.
lessons.q: How does epoll work? Why is it O(1) vs select's O(n)?
lessons.qsub: How does Node.js's libuv use epoll under the hood? Why can Node.js handle 10k concurrent connections on one thread?
terms: Linux ka I/O multiplexing API — kai fds monitor, O(1) event.
Purane APIs — har check par poori list scan (O(n)).
Jab tak data ready, notify deta rehta.
Sirf state change par ek baar notify — data padhna padta.
Node.js ki event-loop library — epoll (Linux) use karta.
lessons.what:
epoll Linux ka way hai kai file descriptors ko ek saath monitor karne ka — "kaunsa ready hai?" Kernel jaanta hai raadhise ready fd, aur aapko sirf ready log deta. Select/poll se better: wo har baar poori list scan karta (O(n)); epoll O(1) — kernel interest-list par event adhiktam dhundhta.

Level-triggered — jab tak data ready, har epoll_wait par notify. Edge-triggered — sirf state change par; aapko sara data padhna hi hoga (warna miss).

Yahi libuv (Node) aur Nginx ka base — ek event loop par 10k+ connections.
lessons.analogy: Gym ka counter / bell system: select/poll = aap har minute har locker check karte (O(n), bekar). epoll = aap register karte ki "ye lockers interest mein hain"; jab koi ready, OS awaaz deta — "locker 5 ready!" (O(1), event). Level = jab tak andar items hain awaaz mehsoos hoti rahe; Edge = sirf jab khola jaye ek baar awaaz — phir aap khud items uthao.
lessons.why: Select/poll ke saath 10k connections = 10k fd ki list har event par scan — slow. epoll kernel-side interest list rakhta, sirf ready fds loutta — responsiveness + scale. Node/Nginx/Redis isi par chalte hain. Interview mein epoll = "how Node handles 10k conns" ka jawab.

lessons.name: How would you build a high-concurrency web server?
lessons.desc: Combines process/thread models, I/O multiplexing, and OS knowledge into a system design.
lessons.q: Design a web server that handles 100,000 concurrent connections. What OS primitives would you use?
lessons.qsub: Compare multi-process (Apache prefork), multi-thread (Apache worker), and event-driven (Nginx) models.
terms: Har request ke liye naya process (fork) — isolated par heavy.
Har request ek thread — lighter than process, shared memory.
lessons.what:
High-concurrency web server design = OS primitives chunna. Teen models:

1. Multi-process (Apache prefork) — Har request ek process (fork). Isolation best par heavy — 10k conns = 10k processes (memory blast).

2. Multi-thread (Apache worker) — Har request ek thread. Lighter (shared memory) par concurrency bugs risk. 10k threads bhi memory-heavy.

3. Event-driven (Nginx/Io node) — Few threads + non-blocking I/O + epoll. Ek event loop hazaron connections ko "ready-event" se handle karta. 10k+ conns, kam memory. Yahi modern answer.
lessons.analogy: Restaurant: process model = har table par ek poori kitchen (isolated but heavy, 100 tables = 100 kitchens). thread = har table ka ek cook jo shared pantry use karta (lighter, par ghool-mel race). event-driven = 1-2 chefs, order note, "ready" bell (event) par serve — chahe 1000 tables hoon, chef rukta nahi, bas ready orders pehchan ke baar-baar serve (epoll).
lessons.why: Interview system-design mein yehi chunna hai: "100k concurrent connections". Process/thread per request scale nahi karta (memory). Event-driven + epoll hi realistic hai. Ye concepts (fork, thread, epoll, non-blocking) OS knowledge ko design se jodte hain — asli "how would you build X" answer.

lessons.name: What happens when you turn on a computer?
lessons.desc: BIOS/UEFI → bootloader → kernel initialization → init/systemd → user processes.
lessons.q: Walk me through what happens from power-on to a running Linux shell.
lessons.qsub: What is GRUB? What does the kernel do during initialization before launching the first process?
terms: Firmware — power on par CPU usse execute karta (self-check).
GRUB — kernel ko memory mein load karta, control deta.
scheduler, memory, drivers setup; rootfs mount.
lessons.what:
Power on → kya hota?:

1. Firmware (BIOS/UEFI) — CPU boot code chalata; hardware self-check; bootable device dhunda.

2. Bootloader (GRUB) — kernel image ko RAM mein load karta, aur uspar control deta. (Jaise main() ko control dena.)

3. Kernel init — memory/paging setup, driver load, root file system mount.

4. init/systemd (PID 1) — pehla user process; baaki services startup karta. Ab aapke paas shell/desktop.
lessons.analogy:
Computer chalana = project kickoff:
1. Reception (firmware) — check sab theek hai, kon si team (device) ready — boot device choose.
2. Manager entrance (bootloader) — manager (kernel) ko stage par latta, "sambhal ab."
3. Manager (kernel) — departments setup (memory, drivers), office (rootfs) kholega.
4. Team lead (init/systemd) — saare employees (services) start hota. Ab kaam (shell) chalna — "boot ho gaya!"
lessons.why: Boot ka chain samajhna = OS ka "hello world" flow. Interview mein "what happens when you turn on computer" — layered architecture dikhata: firmware → bootloader → kernel → user-space. Isi se GRUB, BIOS, PID 1, init concepts saaf hote hain.

lessons.name: What happens when you run a program?
lessons.desc: Loader maps ELF binary, sets up stack/heap, resolves dynamic libraries, jumps to entry point.
lessons.q: Explain what happens at the OS level when you run ./myprogram.
lessons.qsub: What is dynamic linking? What are shared libraries (.so) and why are they better than static linking?
terms: exec ve program file ko memory mein map karta (ELF).
Loader naya process context (stack, heap region) banata.
Shared libraries (.so) load time resolve — save memory/disk.
Program ka pehla instruction (main/_start) jahan control jaata.
lessons.what:
./myprogram chalane par kya hota hai OS level:

1. fork() — naya process banta (parent ki copy). 2. exec() — us process ki image ko myprogram se replace karta. Loader ELF file parh kar code/data ko memory mein map karta, stack+heap setup karta, dynamic libs (.so) resolve karta.

3. Control entry point par jaata — _start/main(). Ab CPGod program chalta hai.

fork + exec: fork naya process banata, exec uski image badalta — two-step Unix design.
lessons.analogy: Apne naye doppelganger (fork) ko banao jo tumhari copy hai; phir usse badal do (exec) ek naye career (program) mein. Loader = HR jo CV (ELF) parh kar desk (memory), kagaz (stack/heap) aur team (libraries) setup karta, phir boss (main) ko bulaata. Dynamic linking = "ye manager library share karte hain" — baar-baar copy nahi (RAM save).
lessons.why: binare, execution ke teen bade OS-fundas milte hain: fork vs exec (process creation), virtual memory mapping (loader), static vs dynamic linking. Interview mein "what happens when you run a program" — inheen deep answers ka test. Isi se shell, ./a.out, libraries ke saare behavior samajhte ho.

lessons.name: What is thrashing?
lessons.desc: Excessive paging — system spends more time swapping pages than executing processes. Working set model prevents it.
lessons.q: What is thrashing? How does the OS detect and prevent it?
lessons.qsub: What is the working set model? How does swappiness tuning affect server performance?
terms: System itna paging kare ki CPU-compute se zyada time swap chale — utilization girti.
Process abhi actively use kar raha pages ka set.
Har unit time kitne faults — badha to problem signal.
Linux: anonymous memory ko swap ki taraf kitna jhukana.
lessons.what:
Thrashing — jab system ke saare processes ke working sets milkar RAM se zyada ho jaate hain. Har process ka page fault rate giri, OS disk se page uthata, par turant hi wo page fir se chahiye → hamesha paging, compute nahi.

Detect — page fault rate bahut zyada, CPU utilization giri. Prevent — working set model: har process ke active pages track; sum > RAM to kuch processes suspend (ya memory badhao). Linux mein swappiness anonymous vs file-cache ka swap rujhan control karta.
lessons.analogy: Overbooked gym: saare members ek saath aaye (too many process), har ek ko machine chahiye (working set). Machine nahi to sab intazaar to intazaar — koi actually exercise nahi kar raha (CPU idle), sab bas "next machine" dhund rahe (faults/swap). Ilaj: kuch members ko suspend kar do (or gym badha do) — tabhi bache exercise (compute) kar paayenge.

lessons.name: Key Linux Internals for Interviews
lessons.desc: /proc filesystem, cgroups, namespaces, copy-on-write — the building blocks of containers.
lessons.q: What are Linux namespaces and cgroups? How do they enable Docker containers?
lessons.qsub: What is the /proc filesystem? What useful information can you extract from /proc/[pid]?
terms: Resources ka izolate view (PID, net, mount) — container ka base.
Pages share, likhte waqt copy — fork/container fast.
Virtual filesystem — kernel/runtime info files mein.
Layered filesystem — image layers, container rootfs.
lessons.what:
Containers (Docker) Linux kernels inheen par bante hain:

Namespaces — processes ko alag views dete (PID, network, mount, user...). Ek container me PID 1, doosre me bhi PID 1 — dono ko apna "isolated system".

cgroups — resource limits (CPU %, memory max). Ek container zyada RAM na le.

Copy-on-write — pages share (fast); likhte hi alp-copy. Fork zaroori binary na copy.

/proc — kernel ka virtual info: /proc/<pid>/ me filenaam, fd, memory, cmdline. OverlayFS — image layers ko merge, rootfs container-specific.
lessons.analogy:
Apartment building ka system:
• Namespace = har flat ko apna "apna flat" lage — sab ka kitchen 101 (PID1), par alag-alag (isolation). Network bhi har flat alag.
• cgroup = property manager limits electricity/water per flat (CPU/memory quota).
• CoW = jab move-in rent (fork), wahan mobile ka furniture (pages) copy nahi — sirf tab jab tab mane.
• /proc = building ka info panel — kaun kaun kahan hai. Image = delivery blueprint.
lessons.why: Ye 4-5 concepts = containers aur Linux internals ka core. Interview mein "how Docker isolate?" ka jawab namespaces+cgroups; "/proc kya?" practical Linux hona. CoW performant fork. Ye modern infra (containers) ko OS se jodte hain — high-signal interview material.

lessons.name: RAID levels — 0, 1, 5, 6, 10, tradeoffs, use cases
lessons.desc: RAID 0: striping (performance, no redundancy). RAID 1: mirroring (redundancy, no performance). RAID 5: striping + distributed parity (3+ disks, single parity). RAID 6: double parity (4+ disks, survives 2 failures). RAID 10: stripe of mirrors (best performance + redundancy, expensive).
lessons.q: What is the difference between RAID 5 and RAID 6? When would you choose each?
lessons.qsub: What is the rebuild time problem with large RAID 5 arrays? How does RAID 10 compare to RAID 5 for write-heavy workloads?
terms: Redundant Array of Independent Disks — kai disks ekaath, performance/reliability.
Data saare disks par split — fast par koi redundancy (1 disk gayi = sab gaya).
Har disk ki copy (mirror) — redundancy, par capacity aadhi, write slow.
Striping + distributed parity — 3+ disks, ek disk fail sahti.
RAID 1 ki pairs + 0 ka stripe — speed + redundancy, expensive.
lessons.what:
RAID kai disks ko milkar use karta hai taaki ya to fast, ya safe (ya dono). Levels alag-alag jhatka-tol:

RAID 0 — data ko strip (blocks) me sab disks par bikhre deta. I/O parallel → fast. Par koi redundancy — ek disk fail to poora data gaya.

RAID 1 — har block ki copy do disks par. Fail-safe, par capacity aadhi.

RAID 5 — strip + parity (recovery info) bant-ta. Ek disk fail par rebuild. RAID 6 — do parity, do fail sahti. RAID 10 — mirror pairs ka stripe = speed + safty (par 2x disk).
lessons.analogy:
Apne important notes ko handle karne ke tarike:
• RAID 0 = notes ko 2 copies se phaad kar do table par rakho — dono padhne tez, par koi bhi table ka page gaya to note adha.
• RAID 1 = dono tables par pura copy — ek table jali tab bhi not mere pass.
• RAID 5 = notes + ek "check-sum" not — ek table gayi to check-sum se baaki reconstruct.
• RAID 10 = har note ke 2 copy pairs, aur unko speed ke liye aranged — behtareen par mehnga.
lessons.why: Storage decisions requirments par: speed (RAID 0), safety (RAID 1), balance (RAID 5/6), best-of-both (RAID10). Rebuild time (bade array) aur write cost parity ka — inheen samajh ke production storage chunoge. HA ke design me yahi answer.

lessons.name: mmap — memory-mapped files, page cache, virtual memory
lessons.desc: mmap maps file contents into virtual memory. OS manages page cache — file reads go through memory. Write-back: modified pages flushed to disk lazily. msync() forces flush. mmap simplifies file I/O but makes memory behavior harder to predict (page faults).
lessons.q: What is mmap and how does it differ from read/write for file I/O?
lessons.qsub: What are the disadvantages of mmap? How does it interact with the page cache?
terms: File ka content memory mein map — virtual memory se file I/O.
Kernel file reads/writes ka cache — memory mein rakhta.
Modified pages lazily disk par flush — bina hari bhari syscalls.
Map-kay hui changes ko force disk par flush.
Access hote hi page load — demand paging.
lessons.what:
mmap — kisi file ko aisi map karo jaisa wo virtual memory ka hissa ho. File par read/write = memory array read/write jaisa (pointer).

OS page cache manage karta — file pages memory mein, access turant. Write-back: badlav lazy disk par jaata (msync force). Page fault pe demand load — pura file nahi, jo chahiye wo pada.

vs read/write: wahan user-space buffer copy hota hai + syscall har baar. mmap se copy kam (memory-mapped access), bade files efficient.
lessons.analogy: Koi badi book (file) padna: read/write = har page ke liye librarian se maango, wo copy deta (syscall + copy). mmap = book ko apne desk par khol ke rakho (map) — seedha padho/likho, koi copy nahi. Jo page chahiye (demand) — use kholo. Apne edits (write-back) book par likho, aur jab chaaho msync se "shelve" kar do (force disk).
lessons.why: Bade files / random access / shared pages ke liye mmap efficient — no per-read syscall copy. Page cache re-use. Isliye DBs (page cache), loaders (map binary), memory-mapped I/O common. Par predictability kam — page faults, memory under pressure (OOM) hard. Interview: "read vs mmap?" ka nuanced answer yahi hai.

lessons.name: Storage device internals — HDD, SSD, NVMe, I/O scheduling
lessons.desc: HDD: spinning platters, seek time (~5-10ms), sequential vs random. SSD: NAND flash, no seek, write amplification, TRIM. NVMe: PCIe interface, much faster than SATA SSD. I/O schedulers: mq-deadline, bfq, none (for fast NVMe). Filesystem choice: ext4, XFS, ZFS.
lessons.q: What is the difference between HDD, SSD, and NVMe at the hardware level?
lessons.qsub: What is write amplification in SSDs? How does TRIM work and why is it important?
terms: Spinning platter + head — seek time (~5-10ms), sequential fast, random slow.
NAND flash, no seek — random fast, write amplification.
SSD over PCIe — bahut fast, low latency, high queue depth.
SSD chhota write bhi bada erase/write karta — wear + slow.
Delete ke baad blocks ko free mark — write amplification kam.
HDD: SCAN-style; NVMe: none/deadline (fast, no magazine).
lessons.what:
HDD — asli spinning disk + magneti head. Data track tak head jaana (seek) = slow ~5-10ms. Sequential tez (ek lahar), random slow (har bar head ghoomta).

SSD — NAND flash, koi moving part, koi seek nahi — random bhi tez. Par write amplification: flash erase hota page-block level, chhota write bhi bada area ab + wear.

NVMe — SSD par PCIe interface — SATA se 4-10x fast, kai queues, deep queue.

TRIM — delete ka block free mark (SSD ki age badhao). I/O scheduler: HDD ko magazine chahiye (SCAN), NVMe ko nahi — none/deadline.
lessons.analogy: Library: HDD = ek librarian jo book ke liye almary tak walk karta (seek). Aas paas ki books (sequential) fast; pichhe-pichhe (random) slow. SSD = books ki chips jahan koi walk nahi — koi bhi book turant (random fast), par har chapter likhne par poore page-block ko doodhna padta (write amplification). NVMe = super-fast conveyor maan lo. TRIM = "ye page free hai" ka sign — likhna asaan.
lessons.why: Modern storage chois samajhna: latency (NVMe <<< SSD < HDD), cost/GB, write pattern, wear. Ye system design, DB, caching ke decisions chalaate hain. SSD wear/write amplification ka meaning — write-heavy ko proper select karna (optane / log) zaroori.

lessons.name: Demand paging — page faults, thrashing, working set
lessons.desc: Demand paging loads pages only when accessed (page fault triggers load from disk). Thrashing: too many page faults → system spends more time paging than computing. Working set: set of pages a process actively uses. Page replacement: LRU, clock algorithm, FIFO.
lessons.q: What is a page fault? What happens when a process accesses a page not in memory?
lessons.qsub: What is thrashing and how do you detect it? How does the working set model prevent thrashing?
terms: Pages tab load karo jab access ho (page fault se) — pura bhari nahi.
Access page RAM mein nahi → router disk se uthata.
Process abhi-kal actively use kar raha pages.
Working sets to > RAM → paging hi paging, compute rukta.
RAM full → kisi page ko evict (LRU/Clock).
lessons.what:
Demand paging — program start hote hi poora memory load nahi karte; jab bhi koi page access hota aur RAM mein nahi, to page fault se disk se uthate hain. Isse memory bacha hota + startup fast (sirf zaroori pages).

Har process ka working set = actively use hone wale pages. Agar saare working sets ka sum RAM se badha → thrashing (har access par fault, CPU khaali). Iska ilaj working set control + page replacement (LRU/Clock) se. Colocation/over-subscribe isi ke aas-paas ghoomta.
lessons.analogy: Ek badi library (program) ko padhna: puri library ek saath jo nahi hoti (demand paging). Tum dekhte (access) ho table 3, 7, 12 — wo hi nikal kar aana (page fault). Jo books abhi-kal use kar rahe ho = working set. Agar sab padhne wale (processes) milkar 100 books maangein aur library me 50 tables (RAM) — to har baar table badalni padegi (thrashing) aur koi actually padh nahi paayega.
lessons.why: Memory limited hai aur programs bade — demand paging se choti RAM par bade programs + fast startup. Par over-subscription par thrashing — performance ka judwa bhut. Working set + LRU/Clock + over-subscribe knobs = production memory management ka core. Interview ka "startup kyun tez" aur "thrashing kya" yahi jawab.

vmstat si/so high → thrashing signal.
Interview: "startup fast?" — lazy page load, sirf zaroori.

lessons.name: POSIX threads (pthreads) — creation, joining, mutex, condition variables
lessons.desc: pthreads is the C/POSIX thread API. pthread_create, pthread_join, pthread_mutex_lock, pthread_cond_wait. Portable across Unix/Linux/macOS. Foundation for understanding OS-level threading. Java threads and Go goroutines build on OS threads which use pthreads on Unix.
lessons.q: How do you create and join a thread using pthreads? What are the key differences from Java threads?
lessons.qsub: How do condition variables work with pthreads? What is spurious wakeup and how do you handle it?
terms: Thread ke khatam hone ka wait (aur result/status lena).
Critical section ka lock — race rokta.
Condition variable — thread "data ready" ka signal.
Bina signal ke thread jag jaata — wait ko loop me lo.
Hardware/OS scheduler se managed — Java threads/Go goroutines isi par (Unix me pthread).
lessons.what:
pthreads = C ka POSIX thread API — Unix/Linux/macOS par OS threads banane ka standard.

pthread_create — thread banata; pthread_join — uske khatam hone ka wait. Sharing: threads ek hi heap/code share karte (unlike process). Isliye mutex zaroori — race se bachne for shared data.

Condition variables — ek thread wait karta jab tak doosra "ready" signal na de (pthread_cond_wait/signal). Spurious wakeup: wait bina signal ke bhi uth sakta — isliye hamesha while loop mein wait karo, if mein nahi.

Java threads / Go goroutines internal OS threads par (Unix par pthreads) use karte — ye base hai.
lessons.analogy:
Ek kitchen team:
• pthread_create = naye cook ko hire karo.
• pthread_join = jab tak wo kaam khatam na kare, main chef wait karta.
• Mutex = ek hi stove (shared), ek time par ek hi cook — lock rakho taaki do do cooks na jale (race).
• Cond var = cook "khana ready" ka signal; doosra wait karta — par "jhootha nagar" (spurious) ho sakta, isliye while loop se phir check karo khana sach mein ready ya nahi.
lessons.why: pthreads = OS-thread programming ka fundamentals. Concurrency, race, synchronization (mutex/condvar) yahi chalti. Java/Go ke "virtual" threads bhi OS threads par banke chalti hain — to ya OS thread model samajhna must. Interview: "thread kya? mutex? deadlock? condvar? spurious?" — sab yahi se.

Shared state natural (heap).
Real parallelism (multicore).
cons: Race/deadlock risk — sync manual.
Context switch / sync overhead.
OS thread count limited (~per process).

Spurious wakeup real hai — hamesha while(!cond) wait.
Java/Go ke threads OS threads par — base to pthreads.
